sources.entry: EnvPane - OS X preference pane for environment variables. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon] ![Freeware][Freeware Icon]](https://github.com/hschmidt/EnvPane)

summary.one_liner: EnvPane is a macOS System Settings-style preference pane for setting per-user environment variables that apply to both GUI and terminal apps, without logging out.
summary.what_it_does: Provides an "Environment Variables" preference pane where you add, edit and delete name/value pairs stored in ~/.MacOSX/environment.plist. A bundled launchd agent runs after login and whenever that file changes, and pushes the variables into the user's launchd instance, so newly launched applications pick them up within a few seconds. It restores the ~/.MacOSX/environment.plist mechanism that Apple dropped after Mountain Lion. Values can interpolate other variables (${NAME} syntax) and the output of shell commands written as $(command), with $$ used for a literal dollar sign. Running applications are not updated and must be relaunched. The README says it cannot set PATH or DYLD_ variables.
use_cases: Set environment variables for all macOS GUI apps
Make shell-style variables available to apps launched from Finder
Interpolate shell command output into environment variable values
Restore environment.plist support on newer macOS
notable: Applies changes to new launches immediately, without reboot or logout
Restores ~/.MacOSX/environment.plist support removed by Apple after Mountain Lion
Supports variable and shell-command interpolation in values
Code-signed universal binary for Intel and Apple Silicon (0.8)
Installs a launchd agent that watches the plist for changes
caveats: Not notarized by Apple, so it is quarantined on download and needs the xattr workaround
Cannot set PATH or DYLD_ variables
Requires macOS 12 Monterey or higher for release 0.8; installs per user only
